evidence.text: The U.S. government announced export restrictions and export licensing requirements targeting China’s semiconductor and supercomputing industries.
evidence.excerpt: In August 2022, the U.S. government, or USG, announced export restrictions and export licensing requirements targeting China’s semiconductor and supercomputing industries.

evidence.text: The restrictions specifically impact NVIDIA's A100 and H100 integrated circuits.
evidence.excerpt: These restrictions impacted exports of certain chips, as well as software, hardware, equipment and technology used to develop, produce and manufacture certain chips to China (including Hong Kong and Macau) and Russia, and specifically impact our A100 and H100 integrated circuits.

evidence.text: In July 2023, the USG informed NVIDIA of an additional licensing requirement for a subset of A100 and H100 products destined to certain customers and other regions.
evidence.excerpt: In July 2023, the USG also informed us of an additional licensing requirement for a subset of A100 and H100 products destined to certain customers and other regions, including some countries in the Middle East.

evidence.text: In October 2023, the USG announced new and updated licensing requirements for exports to China and Country Groups D:1, D:4, and D:5 of NVIDIA's products exceeding certain performance thresholds.
evidence.excerpt: In October 2023, the USG announced new and updated licensing requirements for exports to China and Country Groups D:1, D:4, and D:5 (including but not limited to Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Vietnam, but excluding Israel) of our products exceeding certain performance thresholds.

evidence.text: The licensing requirements apply to the export of products exceeding certain performance thresholds to a party headquartered in Country Group D5, including China.
evidence.excerpt: The licensing requirements also apply to the export of products exceeding certain performance thresholds to a party headquartered in, or with an ultimate parent headquartered in, Country Group D5, including China.

evidence.text: In April 2025, the USG informed NVIDIA that it requires a license for export to China and D:5 countries of H20 integrated circuits.
evidence.excerpt: In April 2025, the USG informed us that it requires a license for export to China (including Hong Kong and Macau) and D:5 countries, or to companies headquartered or with an ultimate parent therein, of our H20 integrated circuits and any other circuits achieving the H20’s memory bandwidth, interconn

evidence.text: NVIDIA incurred a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 associated with H20 for excess inventory and purchase obligations.
evidence.excerpt: As a result of these requirements, we incurred a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 associated with H20 for excess inventory and purchase obligations, as the demand for H20 products diminished.

evidence.text: In August 2025, the USG granted licenses that allowed NVIDIA to ship certain H20 products to certain China-based customers.
evidence.excerpt: In August 2025, the USG granted licenses that would allow us to ship certain H20 products to certain China-based customers.

evidence.text: NVIDIA generated approximately $60 million in H20 revenue under the licenses granted in August 2025.
evidence.excerpt: We generated approximately $60 million in H20 revenue under those licenses.

evidence.text: In February 2026, the USG granted a license that would allow NVIDIA to ship small amounts of H200 products to specific China-based customers.
evidence.excerpt: In February 2026, the USG granted a license that would allow us to ship small amounts of H200 products to specific China-based customers.

evidence.text: NVIDIA has not generated any revenue under the H200 licensing program to date.
evidence.excerpt: To date, we have not generated any revenue under the H200 licensing program, and do not yet know whether any imports will be allowed into China.

evidence.text: The license for H200 products requires that they go through an inspection process in the United States prior to any shipment to the customer.
evidence.excerpt: The license requires that the H200s go through an inspection process in the United States prior to any shipment to the customer.

evidence.text: Any H200 shipped under the new licensing program will be subject to a 25% tariff upon importation into the United States.
evidence.excerpt: As a result, any H200 shipped under the new licensing program will be subject to a 25% tariff upon importation into the United States.

evidence.text: NVIDIA may not be able to pass along all or any of the tariff to its customers if it is able to sell licensed products into the China market.
evidence.excerpt: In the event that we are able to sell licensed products into the China market, we may not be able to pass along all or any of the tariff to our customers, and may be subject to litigation, increased costs, and a harmed competitive position.

evidence.text: NVIDIA is unable to create and deliver a competitive product for China’s data center market that receives approval from both the USG and the Chinese government.
evidence.excerpt: Under the current rules and geopolitical landscape, we are unable to create and deliver a competitive product for China’s data center market that receives approval from both the USG and the Chinese government.

evidence.text: As of the end of fiscal year 2026, NVIDIA was effectively foreclosed from competing in China's data center computing/compute market.
evidence.excerpt: As of the end of fiscal year 2026, we were effectively foreclosed from competing in China's data center computing/compute market.

evidence.text: NVIDIA's effective foreclosure from the China market helped its competitors build larger developer and customer ecosystems to challenge it worldwide.
evidence.excerpt: our effective foreclosure from the China market helped our competitors build larger developer and customer ecosystems to challenge us worldwide.

evidence.text: The USG has imposed worldwide export controls impacting NVIDIA's products.
evidence.excerpt: In addition to controls targeting D:1, D:4 and D:5 countries, the USG has also imposed worldwide export controls impacting our products, and may impose additional controls in the future.

evidence.text: In January 2025, the USG published the AI Diffusion IFR in the Federal Register.
evidence.excerpt: In January 2025, the USG published the AI Diffusion IFR in the Federal Register.

evidence.text: The GAIN AI Act would restrict the Trump Administration’s ability to adapt the Biden Administration’s export control rules.
evidence.excerpt: The GAIN AI Act would restrict the Trump Administration’s ability to adapt the Biden Administration’s export control rules.

evidence.text: NVIDIA's competitive position and future results will be further harmed if the restrictions remain in place or are expanded in geographic, customer, or product scope.
